jobs.description:
The Opportunity:

The Captive Reinsurance Accountant role provides crucial support in the evaluation and management of reinsurance contracts, claims, and relationships with reinsurers. The role is key to ensuring compliance with company policies, efficient claim settlement, and effective communication and collaboration with reinsurers. Additionally, the incumbent will contribute to the generation of insightful reinsurance reports and analysis to support informed decision-making within the organization.



In This Role You Will Execute On:

  • Prepare technical, financial accounting of premium, claim and reserves based on statement of accounts or on bordereaux.

  • Review and analyze reinsurance contracts to ensure adherence to company policies and guidelines.

  • Manage the processing and settlement of reinsurance claims, ensuring accuracy and efficiency.

  • Generate reinsurance reports and conduct analysis to support decision-making.

  • Consult internal stakeholders on Statutory and Reinsurance Accounting expertise and guidance.

  • Develop and maintain effective relationships with reinsurers.

  • Drive continuous process improvement and standardization; actively identify areas for process improvement and inefficiencies.

  • Join relevant training sessions to maintain current relevant knowledge and of the system, processes, and changes.

  • Keep SOP/training guides up to date for role and processes in collaboration with Captive Account Executives.

  • Perform other duties and special projects as requested.



In This Role You Will Need:

  • Bachelor’s degree, preferably Accounting or Finance.

  • Minimum of 3 years of experience in reinsurance accounting, insurance or similar financial area.

  • Proficiency in MS Office, primarily Excel, Outlook, Teams.

  • Skilled at building and maintaining internal and external (carrier) relationships.

  • Strong attention to detail and focus on metrics.

  • Strong interpersonal, written and verbal communication skills; fluent in English.

  • Self-motivated and able to work in a fast-paced environment.

  • Ability and willingness to travel by car or airplane for meetings, conferences, or other business-related functions.



Why Hylant?


Since 1935, Hylant has been a family‑owned insurance brokerage built on relationships, trust, and a people‑first mindset. We believe great work is rooted in understanding people — our clients, our communities, and each other — and delivering thoughtful solutions that rise above the expected.

Anything But Typical. Everything for You. isn’t just a message; it’s how we show up. It reflects a culture where people come first, careers are supported with purpose, and going above and beyond is the standard, not the exception. At Hylant, you’re more than an employee, you’re part of a team that treats one another like family and works together to make a meaningful impact.

About Us

Co-founded in 2023 by Joe Laws and Grant Verstandig, Trase Systems is AI, Uncomplicated. Trase empowers enterprise leaders to harness the full potential of AI without the associated complexity and risks. We are an end-to-end solution for deploying, managing, and optimizing AI in the enterprise. We are leveraging our cutting-edge technologies to develop mission-critical agentic applications in complex industries such as Healthcare, Oil & Gas, and National Security.

About the Role

We are seeking an Engineering Leader to build and lead our Production and Infrastructure Engineering organization. You will manage engineers across DevOps, SRE, DevEx, MLOps, and lead a dedicated support team. You will be accountable for team performance, development, and delivery across these functions.

You will bring a strong foundation in infrastructure and software engineering and stay close enough to the work to challenge assumptions, guide technical decisions, and help engineers resolve difficult problems. Your hands-on involvement will focus on design and code reviews, technical investigation, and pairing when needed, while developing technical leads and delegating implementation to the team.

This role calls for a nimble, adaptable leader who can organize ambiguous work, adjust plans as priorities change, and bring different technical disciplines together around clear outcomes. You will create focus, make timely decisions, and build a team that delivers consistently.

Responsibilities

  • Build and Develop the Team: Own hiring, onboarding, one-on-ones, career development, and performance management. Coach junior engineers, develop technical leads, and give senior specialists clear expectations and candid feedback. Build the skills and ownership needed for the team to operate effectively.
  • Lead Across Technical Disciplines: Set shared priorities and clear responsibilities across infrastructure, reliability, developer experience, testing, and application delivery. Delegate technical execution to the appropriate leads, resolve disagreements, and hold engineers at every level accountable to agreed decisions and commitments.
  • Own Planning and Delivery: Lead sprint planning, backlog grooming, capacity planning, and delivery reviews in partnership with technical leads and TPMs. Turn ambiguous goals into actionable work, manage dependencies and scope, and balance roadmap delivery with incidents and customer support. Replan quickly and communicate tradeoffs when conditions change.
  • Provide Hands-On Technical Leadership: Participate in design and code reviews, ask informed questions, and join investigations or pairing sessions when the team is blocked. Use your infrastructure and software background to connect application behavior with deployment and operational concerns and guide practical solutions.
  • Lead Production and Release Readiness: Make reliability, release and change management, QA, and E2E validation part of the team's delivery process. Assign accountable owners, establish readiness criteria with feature teams, and ensure testing, operational documentation, and rollback plans support release decisions.
  • Strengthen Operations and Developer Experience: Lead the team's improvements to cloud infrastructure, automation, CI/CD, observability, on-call readiness, and incident response. Prioritize work that reduces recurring incidents and developer friction. Use delivery, reliability, recovery, and support metrics to assess results and guide investment.
  • Lead Dedicated Red Cell Partners Support: Manage a cross-functional team of full-stack engineers, DevOps engineers, and a dedicated TPM. Align priorities, staffing, delivery commitments, and support expectations with stakeholders. Resolve dependencies across application and infrastructure teams and maintain clear escalation paths.
  • Partner Across the Organization: Work with Product, Platform, Applied AI, and Security/GRC on delivery priorities, operational readiness, and applicable customer requirements. Surface risks early, secure decisions when needed, and ensure follow-through on engineering commitments.

Requirements

  • Engineering People Leadership: 10+ years of relevant engineering experience, including 5+ years of direct engineering people management, or equivalent demonstrated experience. A track record of building teams, coaching engineers (platform, infrastructure), managing performance, and delivering through technical leads. Director-level candidates should demonstrate leadership across multiple engineering functions.
  • Cross-Functional Execution: Experience leading teams with different technical specialties and seniority levels. Strong planning, prioritization, delegation, and stakeholder communication; able to resolve technical disagreements and keep teams aligned to shared outcomes.
  • Cloud Infrastructure: A strong technical foundation in at least one major cloud platform, such as GCP, AWS, or Azure, with practical experience in Kubernetes, containers, networking, identity, and production operations.
  • Infrastructure as Code and Delivery Automation: Practical experience with Terraform, Git-based development workflows, GitOps, and CI/CD. Able to guide the team's approach to repeatable environments, configuration control, and reliable deployments.
  • Software Engineering: A strong background building and shipping production software, with working depth across backend services, APIs, data stores, and full-stack integration. Able to review code and designs, reason about application failures, and pair with engineers to unblock delivery.
  • Operational and Quality Leadership: Experience leading production delivery and support, including reliability, incident response, release and change management, and collaboration with engineers on automated testing and E2E readiness.
  • Adaptability and Ownership: Demonstrated ability to bring structure to ambiguity, learn unfamiliar technical domains, and make timely decisions with incomplete information. Comfortable shifting between people leadership, delivery issues, and technical discussions while maintaining team focus.
  • Customer and Partner Collaboration: Experience managing technical commitments and escalations with internal or external customers, and translating their needs into feasible priorities and delivery plans.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Familiarity with MLOps, model serving, or operating AI/ML and agent workloads; able to learn from and partner with specialists in these areas.
  • Experience supporting customer-managed environments, multiple cloud providers, or enterprise deployments with complex integration needs.
  • Experience in national security, federal, regulated, or other security-sensitive environments and partnering with Security/GRC on engineering requirements.
  • Experience scaling an engineering organization or building a new team or operating function in a fast-changing company.

Certain national security assignments may require U.S. citizenship and eligibility to obtain and maintain a security clearance, depending on confirmed customer and contract requirements. Some travel is required.

jobs.description:
Our Mission

Healthie is an AI-Native, ONC Certified EHR for modern outpatient healthcare.

Healthie is proud to power clinically excellent healthcare for over 40,000 providers who deliver clinically excellent healthcare - longitudinal and collaboratively, with patient and provider experiences at the center. Both healthcare and technology are undergoing unparalleled industry innovation, and it’s incredible to see the momentum - from consumers, from providers, and from reimbursement for this type of healthcare - grow exponentially.

We provide the powerful infrastructure every care delivery organization needs. On the surface this includes EHR, Scheduling, Engagement, Billing, Data, and much more. Underneath the iceberg are thousands of configurations, settings, widgets, automations, and limitless capabilities because we are an API-first platform. Our fully brandable platform makes it easy for clinics and organizations of any size to scale and never reach a limit.

Today, over 3 billion API calls are made to Healthie every month, as thousands of organizations who work with more than 21 million patients in total, rely on Healthie to deliver clinically excellent healthcare in over 35 specialties, from behavioral healthcare to complex chronic care management and personalized medicine.

We believe in the power of technology to improve access to healthcare and we’re building the rails that make this a reality. We work fast and with quality because we provide business-critical, healthcare-critical software that clinicians and patients need for a better healthcare system. We’re customer-obsessed, operate with lightning-fast processes and responses, and always share our product roadmap publicly- so customers can see what we’re building, and remain relentlessly focused on how care gets delivered.

Healthie is backed by leading investors, and while we've $42M raised to date, more importantly, we operate with fiscal responsibility and have been profitable for more than half of our time as a company. We know that building an ONC-Certified EHR is a lifetime’s body of work, and we are here to build for our customers forever.

Learn more at

About the role

Automate by Healthie gives our customers the ability to set up deterministic, and ultimately agentic, workflows that reduce clicks and streamline operations for clinical care delivery at scale. A simple example is allowing customers to set up a rule “when X happens in a client’s record, do Y” but the potential applications across the surface area of our platform are endless.

You’ll be a founding engineer on this high-velocity, high-impact team that builds, runs, and consistently improves our automations product: the event pipeline, the triggers and actions, and the interface customers use to configure them.

You’re a fit for this role if you have deep customer empathy (product engineering) and enjoy spending time sifting through customer pain points, identifying trends, and implementing opportunities for customers to automate complex clinical and operational processes across the platform.

What You'll Do

  • Build and expand Healthie’s customer-facing workflow automation capabilities, enabling healthcare organizations to automate operational and clinical workflows directly within the Healthie platform.
  • Develop new automation triggers and actions across core product areas, including scheduling, charting, billing, messaging, and patient engagement, helping customers reduce manual work and streamline care delivery.
  • Engineer reliable, scalable automation infrastructure, including retries, idempotency, error handling, failure visibility, and clear customer-facing feedback when automated workflows don't execute as expected.
  • Ship an intuitive, scalable, and error-free Automation builder that enables Healthie customers to create, configure, and manage workflows without requiring technical expertise.
  • Identify and implement opportunities to leverage AI, LLM APIs, and intelligent workflow orchestration to deliver smarter, more adaptive automation capabilities that improve customer efficiency and operational outcomes.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Engineering, Product, Security, and Operations to ensure automation capabilities are secure, scalable, and seamlessly integrated across the Healthie platform.
  • Own the end-to-end technical delivery of customer-facing automation features, from architecture and development through deployment, monitoring, and optimization, while establishing reusable frameworks, engineering standards, and best practices.

About you

  • 8+ years of professional software engineering experience, including significant hands-on experience designing and implementing production-grade automation solutions.
  • Experience building and running event-driven or workflow systems in production, including on-call responsibility for them.
  • Comfort working in Rails or a similar backend framework.
  • Experience handling the unglamorous parts of integration work: webhooks, queues, duplicate events, rate limits, and partial failures.
  • Ability to explain technical tradeoffs to non-engineers, in writing or in person.
  • Experience with cloud infrastructure, preferably AWS, and modern CI/CD tooling.
  • Familiarity with workflow orchestration, job scheduling, event-driven architectures, and automation frameworks.
  • Experience working with relational databases such as PostgreSQL and background processing systems such as Redis or Sidekiq.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently identify opportunities, design technical solutions, and deliver measurable improvements.
  • Strong troubleshooting skills and an understanding of observability, system reliability, and production operations.
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to collaborate across technical and nontechnical teams.

Nice to Have

  • Experience working in healthcare technology, EHR platforms, or other highly regulated environments.
  • Familiarity with HIPAA, healthcare data privacy, and secure automation practices.
  • Experience with Ruby on Rails, React, and GraphQL.
  • Experience with AI-powered development tools, LLM APIs, or building agentic workflow automation tools.
  • Experience automating healthcare workflows involving clinical operations, billing, claims processing, or patient engagement.

Details, details

  • This is a full-time, remote position located within the United States
  • U.S. work authorization is required, Healthie does not provide sponsorship.
  • The base compensation for this position is $190,000 - $220,000.

Interview Process

  • Quick chat with someone from our Talent team (15 min)
  • Interview with Chris, Engineering Manager, (30 minutes)
  • Meet with:
    • Jonathan, VP of Engineering (30 minutes)
    • Cavan, CTO + Cofounder (15 minutes)

jobs.excerpt: OverviewDecisionPoint seeks an Asset / Equipment Specialist to support equipment accountability and asset lifecycle activities for the USMEPCOM ENLIST program.
jobs.description:
Overview

DecisionPoint seeks an Asset / Equipment Specialist to support equipment accountability and asset lifecycle activities for the USMEPCOM ENLIST program. Working under the direction of the Asset Manager, this position supports Hand Receipt Holders (HRHs), the USMEPCOM Property Book Office (PBO), and program teams by maintaining accurate asset records, assisting with physical inventories, tracking maintenance agreements, preparing disposition documentation, and contributing to required asset reports.

The Asset / Equipment Specialist will help ensure that Government-Furnished Property and other program equipment are properly documented throughout receipt, assignment, transfer, maintenance, refresh, return, and disposition. The position requires careful recordkeeping, strong coordination skills, and consistent compliance with Government asset-management procedures.

This position is remote, with Chicago-area candidates preferred. Periodic travel or on-site support may be required for physical inventories, equipment reconciliation, or other program activities.

Note: By applying to this position, you acknowledge and consent to having your resume included in an active competitive government contract bid.

Duties & Responsibilities

The Asset / Equipment Specialist will:

  • Support the Asset Manager, primary Hand Receipt Holders, and the USMEPCOM Property Book Office with equipment accountability activities.
  • Maintain complete and accurate asset records, including serial numbers, asset identifiers, equipment descriptions, locations, assigned custodians, condition, and disposition status.
  • Record and track equipment receipt, assignment, deployment, transfer, refresh, repair, return, and disposition activities.
  • Update Government-designated property, inventory, configuration, or asset-management repositories.
  • Assist with physical asset inventories and audits by verifying equipment identifiers, locations, custodians, operational status, and condition.
  • Document inventory discrepancies and coordinate corrective actions with asset owners, site personnel, and program leadership.
  • Reconcile asset records against shipping, receiving, maintenance, configuration, and disposition documentation.
  • Collect supporting documentation and prepare data tables, findings, and status information for Asset Audit Reports.
  • Track equipment maintenance agreements, warranties, licenses, and support coverage, including renewal and expiration dates.
  • Help prepare equipment disposition packages and maintain supporting approvals, transfer records, shipping documentation, and disposal evidence.
  • Follow Property Book Office guidance for obsolete, excess, surplus, or otherwise disposable Government-Furnished Property.
  • Ensure asset repositories are updated following equipment transfers, returns, replacements, and approved dispositions.
  • Collect and consolidate asset-management metrics, accomplishments, risks, issues, and corrective-action status for Monthly Status Report inputs.
  • Coordinate with logistics, procurement, configuration management, technical support, and site personnel to resolve asset-record discrepancies.
  • Maintain asset-management logs, trackers, checklists, standard operating procedures, templates, and supporting records.
  • Support equipment refreshes, site moves, lifecycle-management activities, and modernization initiatives.
  • Protect sensitive equipment records and handle Government information in accordance with applicable security and records-management requirements.
  • Travel to Government or contractor locations when required to support physical inventories or equipment-accountability activities.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Candidates must meet all of the following requirements:

  • Active Secret clearance or higher.
  • Associate’s degree or relevant professional experience.
  • Minimum of three years of relevant experience in IT asset management, equipment accountability, inventory control, logistics, property administration, or management analysis.
  • Ability to maintain accurate asset records and reconcile equipment information across logs, reports, and supporting documentation.
  • Ability to support physical inventories, asset audits, and equipment-discrepancy resolution.
  • Ability to coordinate effectively with asset custodians, technical teams, and Government stakeholders.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Word, Outlook, and other standard Microsoft Office applications.
  • Strong attention to detail, organizational ability, and written communication skills.
  • Ability to travel or provide on-site support when required for physical inventories or asset-accountability activities.

Preferred Qualifications

The following qualifications are preferred but are not required:

  • Experience supporting federal or Department of Defense property-accountability programs.
  • Experience working with Government-Furnished Property.
  • Familiarity with Hand Receipt Holder and Property Book Office processes.
  • Knowledge of federal or DoD equipment-accountability, transfer, inventory, and disposition requirements.
  • Experience conducting physical asset inventories or supporting Asset Audit Reports.
  • Experience using ServiceNow Hardware Asset Management, Software Asset Management, CMDB, or a comparable asset-management platform.
  • Experience with barcode scanners, RFID tools, or other automated inventory technologies.
  • Experience tracking warranties, maintenance agreements, equipment repairs, and lifecycle status.
  • Experience developing asset metrics and contributing to Monthly Status Reports or similar contract reporting.
  • Experience with Microsoft SharePoint, Teams, Power BI, or related collaboration and reporting tools.
  • ITIL Foundation, Certified Hardware Asset Management Professional, Certified IT Asset Manager, or another relevant asset-management certification.

Skills and Competencies

  • Excellent recordkeeping and data-quality skills.
  • Strong organizational and time-management abilities.
  • Ability to reconcile detailed information from multiple systems and source documents.
  • Ability to follow established asset-management procedures and escalation paths.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to coordinate effectively across remote and geographically dispersed teams.
  • Sound judgment when handling Government property records and sensitive information.
  • Ability to manage multiple assignments, deadlines, and follow-up actions.
  • Commitment to accuracy, accountability, and consistent process execution.

Our Equal Employment Opportunity Policy

  • EEO and Affirmative Action Policy: DecisionPoint Corporation is an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer. It is the policy of DecisionPoint Corporation to provide equal employment opportunity in accordance with all applicable Equal Employment Opportunity/Affirmative Action laws, directives and regulations to all employees and qualified applicants without regard to race, ethnicity, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, disability status, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other protected status under Federal, State or Local laws.
  • Pay Transparency Policy: In accordance with Presidential Executive Order 13665, DecisionPoint Corporation will not discharge or in any other manner discriminate against employees or applicants because they have inquired about, discussed, or disclosed their own pay or the pay of another employee or applicant. However, employees who have access to the compensation information of other employees or applicants as a part of their essential job functions cannot disclose the pay of other employees or applicants to individuals who do not otherwise have access to compensation information, unless the disclosure is (a) in response to a formal complaint or charge, (b) in furtherance of an investigation, proceeding, hearing, or action, including an investigation conducted by the employer, or (c) consistent with the contractor's legal duty to furnish information.

IonQ, Inc. [NYSE: IONQ] is the world’s leading quantum platform and merchant supplier - delivering integrated quantum solutions across computing, networking, sensing, and security. IonQ’s newest generation of quantum computers, the IonQ Tempo, is the latest in a line of cutting-edge systems that have been helping customers and partners including Amazon Web Services, and AstraZeneca achieve 20x performance results and accelerate innovation in drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling, logistics, cybersecurity, and defense. Headquartered in College Park, Maryland, IonQ has operations in California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Tennessee, Washington, Italy, South Korea, Sweden, Switzerland, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Our quantum computing services are available through all major cloud providers, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. Director, Community Management

College Board - Operations

Location:

  • This is a remote role. Candidates who live near CB offices have the option of being fully remote or hybrid (Tuesday and Wednesday in office). All CB employees are required to occasionally travel to meet in person for business purposes.

Role Type:

  • This is a full-time position

About the Team

College Board's Operations division is a best-in-class digital assessment delivery and customer engagement function that supports millions of students and thousands of test centers, annually. The Operations team is also leading exciting work to advance user experience using innovative solutions, products, and technology to enhance the end-to-end delivery of digital assessments and all aspects of customer support. Within Operations, the Assessment Delivery Operations (ADO) team is responsible for the successful execution of digital assessments like the SAT and Advanced Placement (AP) examinations, working closely with partners across College Board, the education sector, and beyond to improve testing technologies, customer experience, and outcomes. ADO’s User Readiness team ensures every district-level member, school-level educator, and test taker has what they need, and takes the critical actions required, to succeed on test day. This is done through multi-channel community engagement, effective digital communications, curated technical guidance, and risk-based outreach.

About the Opportunity

As a Director of Community Management, you will own on-demand support and resources for College Board's user communities, including the digital channels, peer programs, and always-available resources that keep district and school-level staff informed and engaged between live touchpoints. You will help sustain and expand AP's on-demand coordinator experience, including its peer ambassador program, digital content channels, and community platform, partnering closely with a peer who oversees a portfolio of high-touch coordinator programming. You will also help design and scale a model that can extend beyond AP to other College Board assessment types, identifying where a shared, cross-program approach serves a wide range of educators supporting College Board high-stakes assessments globally. The durable, trust-based relationships you build with test coordinators and staff will reduce risk before it ever requires intervention, ensuring a seamless testing experience for staff and students.

In this role, you will:

Coordinate Community Programs (35%)

  • Own the New AP Coordinator Outreach Program end-to-end, directing staffing, training, and budget strategy, and using escalations and survey/readout data to continuously refine the program
  • Own the AP Coordinator Champions program, from identifying, vetting, and validating candidates through recruiting, onboarding, training design, and ongoing engagement, including contract and expense management
  • Shapes the AP Coordinator Community strategy, overseeing content, resources, and escalations, and drives engagement in partnership with dedicated coordinator support consultant teams

Content, Channels & Resources (40%)

  • Own portfolio-level communication strategy, including daily news and seed-list content and coordination across the 15+ available cross-program promotion channels
  • Owns the strategy and lifecycle of annual coordinator resources, leading continuous improvement year-over-year

Community Strategy & Growth (25%)

  • Identify and build the operating model, staffing approach, and playbook to scale this community function beyond AP as College Board's community engagement needs grow
  • Design and deliver segment-tailored engagement across the full spectrum from high-touch to self-serve, so every coordinator population gets the model of support that fits need
  • Partner with operational, learning and development, and program partners to turn coordinator voice-of-customer and experiment results into segment strategy, risk definitions, and cross-program priorities

About You

  • A combination of education and experience equal to 5-7 years managing community, content campaigns, or digital engagement programs, including direct experience with volunteer, ambassador, or peer-community programs
  • Experience owning digital content channels end to end (e.g., YouTube, podcast, or similar platforms), including production, analytics, sound engineering, and channel strategy
  • A track record of designing and scaling communication programs across multiple channels and audiences
  • Experience translating user or customer feedback into concrete changes to strategy, content, or programming
  • A proven ability to influence and align stakeholders without direct authority, building buy-in across program partners to move shared priorities forward
  • Comfort operating in ambiguity, including building a scalable, multi-program model from a program-specific starting point
  • Strong project management skills, including managing budgets, contracts, and vendor or volunteer relationships
  • The ability to travel 5-10 times per year to College Board offices or on behalf of College Board business
  • Experience supporting high-stakes assessment or test delivery operations (preferred)
  • A customer service or customer experience background (preferred)

All roles at College Board require:

  • A passion for expanding educational and career opportunities and mission-driven work
  • Curiosity and enthusiasm for emerging technologies, with a willingness to experiment with and adopt new AI-driven solutions and comfort with learning and applying new digital tools independently and proactively.
  • Clear and concise communication skills, written and verbal
  • A learner's mindset and a commitment to growth: welcoming diverse perspectives, giving and receiving timely, respectful feedback, and continuously improving through iterative learning and user input.
  • A drive for impact and excellence: solving complex problems, making data-informed decisions, prioritizing what matters most, and continuously improving through learning, user input, and external benchmarking.
  • A collaborative and empathetic approach: working across differences, fostering trust, and contributing to a culture of shared success
  • Authorization to work in the United States

About Our Process

  • Application review will begin immediately and will continue until the position is filled. This role is expected to accept applications for a minimum of 5 business days.
  • While the hiring process may vary, it generally includes: resume and application submission, recruiter phone/video screen, hiring manager interview, performance exercise such as live coding, a panel interview, a conversation with leadership and reference checks.

What We Offer

At College Board, we offer more than a paycheck: we provide a meaningful career, a supportive team, and a comprehensive package designed to help you thrive. We’re a self-sustaining nonprofit that believes in fair and competitive compensation grounded in your qualifications, experience, impact, and the market.

A Thoughtful Approach to Compensation

  • The hiring range for this role is $80,000–$130,000
  • Your exact salary will depend on your location, experience, and how your background compares to others in similar roles at the College Board.
  • We aim to make our best offer upfront, rooted in fairness, transparency, and market data.
  • We adjust salaries by location to ensure fairness, no matter where you live.

You’ll have open, transparent conversations about compensation, benefits, and what it’s like to work at College Board throughout your hiring process. Check out our careers page for more.

Job Title: Front-End Developer
Location: Fully Remote (US)

About Edconic

Edconic is a leading player in the alternative, experiential education space. We partner with the world's largest and most well-known brands to create and run schools that capture the legacy and value of each brand. Our students get truly unique, once-in-a-lifetime experiences that help shape their future and give them the skills they need to reach their goals.

The Role

We're looking for an experienced Front-End Developer to join our web team, which owns every Edconic digital property – from our school websites to landing pages and email templates. You'll work alongside designers, IT, and MarTech to build solutions that serve real business needs while protecting each brand's unique identity.

You'll be one of two developers on the team, working directly with our lead developer. That means real ownership of your work, a genuine voice in how we build, very little process overhead, and a codebase that is actively moving toward a modern, standardized WordPress stack. We value craft: fast pages and code that the next developer can read.

What You'll Do

  • Build and maintain public-facing websites, micro-sites, and landing pages in collaboration with our lead developer, IT, and MarTech.
  • Work with UX/UI designers to confirm the technical feasibility of designs, then translate them into polished, responsive pages that stay true to each brand.
  • Build and maintain custom WordPress themes across both of our stacks: modern block-based builds (ACF Blocks, core blocks, block patterns, theme.json) and established classic themes built on PHP templates, Advanced Custom Fields, and Sass.
  • Collaborate with our lead developer to shape the team's coding standards, tooling, and workflow, and help migrate our existing sites toward our new modern stack.
  • Stay current on emerging web standards and bring ideas to the table where they genuinely fit.

What You Bring

  • 4+ years of front-end web development experience, with strong skills in semantic HTML, CSS, JavaScript, PHP, and WordPress.
  • The ability to build a custom WordPress theme from scratch using PHP templates and Advanced Custom Fields.
  • Strong CSS skills across Sass and modern native CSS (custom properties, nesting), and solid vanilla JavaScript.
  • Comfort working in Git/GitHub with pull requests and code reviews, and with npm-based build tools and the command line.
  • A habit of writing semantic, well-structured HTML that covers accessibility basics, with an eye for reuse, cross-browser compatibility, performance, and SEO.
  • Experience building and testing HTML emails.
  • Strong UX/UI sensibilities and a desire to sweat the small stuff.
  • A proactive, self-directed working style – you can run with a project independently and prioritize across several at once.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication – you're positive, collaborative, objective, and solution-oriented.

Bonus Experience

  • Modern WordPress block development: ACF Blocks, block.json, theme.json, and block patterns.
  • Composer, Bedrock or other Roots tooling (Sage/Blade, Trellis), Vite, or CI/CD with GitHub Actions.
  • Deeper accessibility experience (WCAG, ARIA, assistive-technology testing).
  • CRM and marketing automation integration (Salesforce, Pardot/Account Engagement).
  • Multilingual WordPress sites.
  • A modern JavaScript framework such as React or Vue.
  • UX or UI design, and design tools such as Figma and Adobe Creative Suite.

How We Use AI

AI-assisted development is a new and evolving part of our workflow. We use AI coding tools to speed up research, scaffolding, review, and routine work, and you're welcome to do the same.

AI is a tool here, not a substitute for expertise. You are accountable for every line of code that you ship, which means you must be able to write, review, debug, and explain production code entirely on your own. Expect to demonstrate those skills without AI assistance during the interview process.

Location, Travel & Eligibility

  • Fully remote within the United States. Occasional travel to our New York office may be required.
  • Must be legally authorized to work in the US.
  • Bachelor's degree preferred (Computer Science, Interaction Design, Graphic Design, Communications, or a related field); equivalent professional experience is equally welcome.

Our Commitment

Edconic supports and embraces diversity and inclusiveness, and we encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply, even if you don't meet every requirement listed here. Reasonable accommodations are available to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the role and to participate in the interview process.

The above statements describe the general nature and level of work for this position. They are not an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, and skills. Edconic reserves the right to modify this job description at its sole discretion.

jobs.excerpt: À propos de ShareGateShareGate est le leader en migration et gouvernance Microsoft 365, avec plus de 100 000 professionnels TI qui comptent sur sa simplicité imbattable.
jobs.description:
À propos de ShareGate

ShareGate est le leader en migration et gouvernance Microsoft 365, avec plus de 100 000 professionnels TI qui comptent sur sa simplicité imbattable.

Il offre l’approche la plus simple, fiable et abordable pour migrer les données d’entreprise sur Microsoft 365.

Que ce soit Google Workspace, les disques réseaux, Exchange Online, SharePoint On-Premises, ou d’un tenant à l’autre, ShareGate s’en occupe et offre la paix d’esprit. D’une transition vers le cloud à l’intégration d’une nouvelle entreprise, il garde les choses vraiment simples.

ShareGate est aussi l’outil de prédilection pour garder le contrôle des données une fois que la migration est complétée. Ses fonctionnalités de gouvernance permettent d'évaluer rapidement les environnements M365, détecter les problèmes et apporter les correctifs nécessaires, pour que tout reste ordonné, sécurisé et optimisé. Il aide à mettre en place la fondation pour déployer avec confiance l’assistant d'IA de Microsoft.

ShareGate est développé par Workleap Technologies, une entreprise de logiciels basée à Montréal.

Ton rôle

Tu seras responsable de la façon dont Workleap détecte les menaces, enquête et y répond, chez Workleap comme chez ShareGate, et tu bâtiras la couche d'IA qui fait tourner tout ça. Nos outils de sécurité génèrent plus de bruit qu'une petite équipe peut en traiter, et trop de constats sont ambigus ou erronés. Ce rôle existe maintenant pour transformer la détection et la réponse en un système où des agents trient, enrichissent et enquêtent, et où les humains prennent les décisions qui demandent vraiment du jugement. C'est un rôle de contributeur.trice individuel.le de niveau Staff, très concret, sans gestion d'équipe.

Ton impact :

  • Bâtir le pipeline qui fait tourner les opérations de sécurité de bout en bout : les intégrations qui extraient les alertes et les constats de chaque outil source, un système agentique qui les trie, les enrichit, les corrèle et rédige l'enquête, et une connexion à Jira qui achemine chaque résultat vers l'équipe responsable avec les preuves et une voie de correction, pour qu'aucun constat ne soit jamais recopié à la main ;
  • Définir le modèle de confiance de ces agents : ce qu'ils ferment seuls, ce qu'ils recommandent et ce qui revient toujours à un humain, appuyé par des evals et protégé contre l'injection de prompt et l'abus de permissions ;
  • Éliminer les faux positifs et les constats mal évalués de nos outils de sécurité, pour que chaque constat qui arrive à une personne soit réel et bien priorisé ;
  • Piloter l'ingénierie de détection de bout en bout, écrite sous forme de code et alignée sur MITRE ATT&CK, pour que la couverture survive à tout changement de plateforme ;
  • Mener la réponse aux incidents de sécurité, du triage au postmortem, avec des agents qui rassemblent les preuves, et tenir notre partenaire de détection gérée à un standard mesurable ;
  • Faire de la sécurité un partenaire que les équipes de développement veulent avoir, en livrant les constats dans leur flux de travail avec des preuves claires et une voie de correction.

Ton équipe

Au cours des 12 prochains mois, LeapSec livre deux paris stratégiques : intégrer la sécurité dans les squads produit, avec des agents qui portent le travail de vulnérabilités et de détection, et automatiser la collecte de preuves SOC 2 pour que personne n'ait à la faire à la main. Tu seras responsable du volet détection et réponse : nettoyer l'outillage, bâtir les agents et démontrer jusqu'où on peut leur faire confiance.

LeapSec regroupe les Opérations de sécurité et la Conformité pour Workleap et ShareGate. Tu relèveras du directeur Infrastructure et Sécurité et tu travailleras au quotidien avec notre spécialiste Staff en sécurité applicative et l'équipe d'outillage de sécurité, et au besoin avec l'Infrastructure, l'ITX et l'ingénierie produit. On est une petite équipe avec un large mandat : on suit le travail honnêtement dans Jira, on livre à dates fixes et on s'attend à ce que chacun.e prenne ses résultats en charge de bout en bout.

Notre environnement est d'abord Azure, avec aujourd'hui une plateforme SIEM et XDR infonuagique, Zscaler, Cloudflare et un partenaire de détection gérée. On choisit nos outils au mérite et on compte continuer à le faire.

Ce que tu apportes

  • La maîtrise de l’anglais est requise, car tu vas collaborer régulièrement avec des collègues, des clients et des partenaires qui parlent une autre langue que le français;
  • 7 ans et plus en opérations de sécurité, réponse aux incidents ou ingénierie de détection, avec une expérience pratique récente dans un environnement SaaS infonuagique ;
  • Une solide expérience des constats qui ne sont pas clairs : valider ce que les outils signalent, éliminer les faux positifs à la source et trancher, avec des preuves incomplètes, si quelque chose est réel ;
  • Des années à travailler directement avec des équipes de développement, à faire livrer des correctifs sans autorité formelle et à préserver la relation quand la réponse est non ;
  • De l'expérience à bâtir et déployer des systèmes d'agents pour la sécurité dont d'autres dépendent, comme des serveurs MCP, des skills Claude ou des outils sur mesure, avec des evals qui déterminent quand leurs résultats sont fiables ;
  • Une bonne compréhension de la façon dont les systèmes agentiques échouent et sont attaqués, notamment l'injection de prompt, la gestion des permissions des outils et des identifiants ;
  • L'ingénierie de détection comme discipline : détections sous forme de code, un langage de requête SIEM que tu maîtrises et des taux de faux positifs réellement mesurés ;
  • Une solide compréhension des chemins d'attaque liés à l'identité et à l'infonuagique, idéalement dans Azure et Entra ID ;
  • Atout : expérience à diriger un partenaire de détection gérée, en chasse aux menaces ou en forensique, et aisance en français.

La plupart de cela te ressemble ? Postule.

Ce que le poste inclut

jobs.title: Information System Security Officer (ISSO)
jobs.excerpt: OverviewLMI is seeking an Information System Security Officer (ISSO) to support the Robotics and Autonomous Systems (RAS) business unit and Department of War mission partners.
jobs.description:
Overview

LMI is seeking an Information System Security Officer (ISSO) to support the Robotics and Autonomous Systems (RAS) business unit and Department of War mission partners. The ISSO will maintain system security documentation, coordinate Risk Management Framework (RMF) activities, support Authority to Operate (ATO) packages, and track security controls, vulnerabilities, and remediation actions throughout the system lifecycle.

The ISSO will work with the Information System Security Manager (ISSM), government system owners, assessors, and engineering teams to keep authorization records aligned with deployed systems. The ideal candidate combines hands-on DoD authorization experience with the technical judgment to evaluate evidence, identify security gaps, and coordinate corrective actions.

This remote position requires an active Secret security clearance and the ability to obtain and maintain Top Secret if required by the assignment. Periodic travel may be required for assessments, customer meetings, and access to approved facilities. All classified work must be performed in approved facilities.

LMI is a new breed of digital solutions provider dedicated to accelerating government impact with innovation and speed. Investing in technology and prototypes ahead of need, LMI brings commercial-grade platforms and mission-ready AI to federal agencies at commercial speed.

Leveraging our mission-ready technology and solutions, proven expertise in federal deployment, and strategic relationships, we enhance outcomes for the government efficiently and effectively. With a focus on agility and collaboration, LMI serves the defense, space, healthcare, and energy sectors, helping agencies navigate complexity and outpace change. Headquartered in Tysons, Virginia, LMI is committed to delivering impactful results that strengthen missions and drive lasting value.

Responsibilities

  • Maintain System Security Plans, control implementation statements, system inventories, authorization boundaries, network and data-flow diagrams, and supporting records in eMASS or another customer-approved system.
  • Support system categorization, control selection, and documentation of inherited and system-specific controls, including shared responsibilities across cloud providers, platform teams, and application owners.
  • Prepare and maintain authorization packages for initial authorization, renewal, and system changes; coordinate evidence collection, reviews, assessment milestones, and responses to findings.
  • Maintain Plans of Action and Milestones (POA&Ms), assign and track remediation actions with responsible teams, and document validation and closure evidence.
  • Review vulnerability scans, Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG) checklists, and security advisories; coordinate remediation and document unresolved risks for appropriate review.
  • Execute the approved continuous monitoring plan, coordinating control reviews, scan schedules, account reviews, audit-log reviews, configuration checks, and required reporting.
  • Evaluate proposed changes to applications, infrastructure, interfaces, and data flows for security impacts; update documentation and coordinate any additional assessment or authorization requirements.
  • Work with cloud, platform, software, and cybersecurity engineers to collect technical evidence from deployed systems and software delivery pipelines, including configuration and vulnerability results.
  • Support security assessments, inspections, and audits by organizing evidence, responding to assessor questions, and tracking corrective actions through resolution.
  • Maintain security procedures and support access-control reviews, incident reporting, contingency planning, and recovery exercises in coordination with responsible technical and security teams.
  • Provide status reports on authorization milestones, monitoring results, vulnerabilities, and overdue actions; elevate risk recommendations to the ISSM and authorized government decision-makers.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

  • Active Secret security clearance, with the ability to obtain and maintain Top Secret if required by the assignment.
  • Minimum of five years of relevant experience as an ISSO, ISSM, cybersecurity compliance professional, or equivalent practitioner supporting DoD information systems.
  • Demonstrated hands-on experience preparing and maintaining DoD RMF authorization packages, including security control documentation, assessment support, POA&M management, and ATO sustainment.
  • Experience using eMASS, Xacta, or a comparable government authorization system to maintain control responses, assessment evidence, findings, and authorization records.
  • Working knowledge of NIST SP 800-53 security controls, DISA STIGs, vulnerability management, continuous monitoring, and DoD system authorization requirements.
  • Ability to interpret vulnerability scan results, technical configurations, system diagrams, and assessment findings, and coordinate evidence-based remediation with engineers and system owners.
  • Working knowledge of operating systems, networking, identity and access management, encryption, configuration management, and logging sufficient to evaluate security-control implementation.
  • Current cybersecurity certification relevant to the assigned duties and ability to meet applicable DoD 8140 work-role and proficiency-level qualification requirements within customer-required timelines.
  • Strong technical writing, documentation, organization, and stakeholder coordination skills; ability to manage concurrent deadlines, protect sensitive information, and work independently within a distributed team.
  • Ability to support periodic travel and perform classified duties at approved facilities. A college degree is not required.

Desired Qualifications:

  • Experience supporting authorizations for cloud-hosted systems in AWS GovCloud, Azure Government, or another government-authorized cloud environment, including control inheritance and shared-responsibility documentation.
  • Experience supporting systems at DoD Impact Level 4, 5, or 6, including mission applications, data platforms, or environments supporting robotics and autonomous systems.
  • Familiarity with Kubernetes, containers, DevSecOps, automated security evidence, software supply-chain controls, or security requirements for onboarding applications to an authorized platform.
  • Experience supporting Special Operations Forces, combatant commands, military service components, or Intelligence Community mission partners.
  • Experience supporting independent security control assessments or implementing continuous monitoring processes across multiple systems.
  • CGRC, CISSP, CISM, or a related advanced cybersecurity certification.
  • Bachelor's or master's degree in cybersecurity, information systems, computer science, or a related discipline.

The target salary range for this position is $92,075 - $158,138.

The salary range displayed represents the typical salary range for this position and is not a guarantee of compensation. Individual salaries are determined by various factors including, but not limited to location, internal equity, business considerations, client contract requirements, and candidate qualifications, such as education, experience, skills, and security clearances.  

Applicants must meet eligibility requirements for a U.S. Government security clearance. Only US Citizens are eligible for a security clearance. For this position, LMI will only consider applicants with security clearances or applicants who are eligible for security clearances, due to the nature of the work.

About the Role

WEX is reimagining its enterprise data platform with an ambitious goal: make our data understandable not only to people and applications, but also to AI models and autonomous agents.

We are looking for a Senior Director to lead the next generation of our Data-as-a-Service (DaaS) platform and build the semantic foundation that connects data with its business meaning.

This leader will define and drive how WEX creates trusted semantic objects for our major business domains—such as customers, accounts, merchants, transactions, vehicles, payments, claims, and risk signals. These objects will bring together data, relationships, business definitions, derived attributes, policies, lineage, and context into reusable assets that can power analytics, data products, decisioning, and AI experiences.

This is a highly visible leadership role. You will lead a team of senior engineers and technical leaders while partnering closely with Product, AI, Analytics, Risk, Finance, and business teams across WEX.

The space is evolving quickly. We are not looking for someone who has already built an exact version of this platform. We are looking for a leader with deep data and platform experience, strong technical judgment, and the ability to help invent what the next generation of enterprise data platforms should become in an AI-native world.

How you'll make an impact

  • Define the technical vision, architecture, and multi-year roadmap for WEX's semantic data platform and next generation of Data as a Service.

  • Build semantic business objects that bring together enterprise data, business context, relationships, metrics, derived attributes, rules, lineage, quality, and governance.

  • Establish a scalable approach for creating semantic objects across WEX's different lines of business while maintaining consistent enterprise standards.

  • Lead development of platform capabilities across semantic modeling, ontology, metadata, knowledge graphs, data quality, lineage, data contracts, and governance.

  • Partner deeply with business and product leaders to capture business meaning that today may live across databases, applications, workflows, documents, spreadsheets, policies, and institutional knowledge.

  • Enable AI and agentic applications to discover, understand, reason over, and safely act on trusted enterprise data.

  • Build reusable platform capabilities and developer experiences that allow teams to create new data products and AI experiences faster.

  • Lead and develop a high-performing organization of engineers, architects, and senior technical leaders.

  • Partner with Principal and Staff engineers to establish architectural standards and solve complex distributed data and platform problems.

  • Drive adoption across engineering and business teams, ensuring the platform delivers measurable customer and business outcomes—not simply new technology.

Experience you'll bring

  • 15+ years of experience in software engineering, data engineering, distributed systems, data platforms, or related technology areas, including significant technical leadership experience.

  • Experience leading engineering organizations responsible for large-scale data, platform, infrastructure, or developer capabilities.

  • Deep understanding of modern data architecture, including large-scale data processing, streaming, lakehouse architectures, data products, and distributed systems.

  • Deep understanding of semantic data technologies and industry direction is essential. Direct experience building a semantic data layer is strongly recommended.

  • Demonstrated ability to translate complex business concepts into scalable technical abstractions and reusable platform capabilities.

  • Strong understanding of data quality, governance, lineage, security, privacy, and operational reliability.

  • Experience building platforms adopted by multiple engineering teams, business domains, or product organizations.

  • Strong architectural judgment with the ability to evaluate tradeoffs and move comfortably between long-term strategy and detailed technical discussions.

  • Demonstrated ability to influence senior technical, product, and business leaders across organizational boundaries.

  • Experience hiring, mentoring, and developing senior engineering talent and technical leaders.

  • Strong communication skills with the ability to explain complex technical concepts to engineering teams, business partners, and executive leadership.

Preferred experience

  • Experience building platforms that support AI/ML, generative AI, RAG, or agentic applications.

  • Experience with knowledge representation, semantic search, context engineering, graph technologies, or AI-ready enterprise data.

  • Experience modernizing large enterprise data ecosystems with multiple business domains and legacy systems.

  • Experience driving a significant platform transformation from concept through enterprise adoption.

The most important qualification is not familiarity with a particular tool or architecture. We are looking for a leader who can combine deep engineering expertise, business understanding, and first-principles thinking to help define how enterprise data should work in an AI-native future.

jobs.excerpt: Founded in 2012, Bugcrowd is the preemptive security platform that unifies exposure discovery and assessment, offensive testing, and intelligence shaped by AI and human insight to help organizations avoid, discover, and validate real-world risk.
jobs.description:
Founded in 2012, Bugcrowd is the preemptive security platform that unifies exposure discovery and assessment, offensive testing, and intelligence shaped by AI and human insight to help organizations avoid, discover, and validate real-world risk. Bugcrowd helps security teams move faster by identifying the exposures that matter most so they can act first and stay ahead of attackers. By combining the power of humans and AI, teams can preempt attack paths and prevent breaches. Based in San Francisco and New Hampshire, Bugcrowd is supported by General Catalyst, Rally Ventures, Costanoa Ventures, and others. Visit .

Job Summary

The Bugcrowd RL and Reasoning Team focuses on pushing the boundaries of autonomous cybersecurity by building authentic, verifiable reinforcement learning environments for world-leading foundational AI companies. As a Reinforcement Learning Engineer specializing in Reinforcement Learning from Verifiable Rewards (RLVR), you will design and scale automated verification pipelines that transform real-world software vulnerabilities into deterministic reward functions. In this role, you will bridge the gap between low-level security analysis and modern LLM reasoning models, engineering environments where AI agents learn to discover, exploit, and remediate software vulnerabilities with mathematical certainty. Instead of relying on subjective human feedback, your work directly powers the rigorous, verifiable reward signals that teach next-generation frontier AI models how to master complex cybersecurity domain logic. You will work at the intersection of fuzzing, dynamic program analysis, system exploitation, and scalable ML infrastructure to shape the safety and offensive/defensive capabilities of future artificial intelligence.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Design, build, and deploy high-throughput RLVR (Reinforcement Learning from Verifiable Rewards) environments that evaluate LLM action sequences against deterministic execution outcomes.
  • Develop automated test harnesses, sandboxes, and verification engines that convert complex vulnerability research (e.g., memory corruption, web security, logic bugs) into binary pass/fail reward signals.
  • Integrate Bugcrowd’s Mayhem automated analysis platform and real-world vulnerability feeds into continuous, scalable RL environment generation pipelines.
  • Architect safe, isolated, and highly reproducible execution environments (using Docker, BuildKit, or Nix) capable of running thousands of simultaneous agent-driven exploitation and patching trajectories.
  • Collaborate directly with researchers at frontier AI labs including Anthropic, OpenAI, and Cohere to define standard benchmark formats, observation spaces, and verifiable evaluation metrics for cybersecurity tasks.
  • Implement precise telemetry, ground-truth verification algorithms, and trajectory logging to analyze agent reasoning paths and prevent reward hacking or false positives.
  • Build low-level instrumentation and debugging tools to monitor memory states, process executions, and network behaviors during agent interaction cycles.
  • Optimize infrastructure performance and environment reset latency to support massive-scale parallel sampling and distributed RL training workflows.
  • Benchmark and evaluate frontier AI model performance across diverse offensive and defensive security challenges, such as automated fuzzing, exploit payload generation, and patch validation.

Education, Experience, Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Understanding of RL training workflows used by modern LLM systems, specifically execution-based feedback or Reinforcement Learning from Verifiable Rewards (RLVR).
  • Proficiency developing applications in Python and low-level systems programming in C, with Rust experience being a strong plus.
  • Solid understanding of software vulnerabilities, binary exploitation, fuzzing methodologies, or program analysis.
  • Experience with DevOps pipelines (e.g., GitHub Actions), reproducible builds (Docker, BuildKit, Nix), and comfort working with Linux systems and low-level debugging.
  • Experience working with or building benchmark environments (e.g., CTFs, SWE-bench, security challenges, or execution sandboxes).

Preferred Experience

  • Experience designing custom reward functions, ground-truth verifiers, or automated grading engines for AI safety and reasoning models.
  • Background in low-level program analysis tools, sanitizers (e.g., ASan/MSan), compiler instrumentation, or automated exploit generation tools.
  • Proven track record of participating in or developing competitive cybersecurity benchmarks, CTFs, or open-source AI evaluation frameworks.

Working Conditions and Physical Requirements

The ideal candidate must be able to complete all physical requirements of the job with or without reasonable accommodation.

Sitting and / or standing - Must be able to remain in a stationary position 50% of the time

Carrying and / or lifting - Must be able to carry / move laptop as needed throughout the work day.

Environment - remote, work-from-home 100% of the time.

Pay Range Disclosure

At Bugcrowd, we strive for fairness, equality and to create an environment that allows our people to perform at their very best. Our compensation philosophy is to foster a collaborative community that rewards, attracts and retains the best possible talent. The provided salary details are based on US national averages and we retain the flexibility to tailor to the needs of the business.

The national estimate for the current base range for the position of $176,400 - $242,550.

This position may also be eligible to participate in a discretionary bonus program or commission plan, subject to the rules governing the program, whereby an award, if any, depends on various factors, including, without limitation, individual and organizational performance.

Culture

  • At Bugcrowd, we understand that diversity in the workplace is vital to a company’s success and growth. We strive to make sure that people are included and have a sense of being part of making Bugcrowd not only a great product but a great place to work.
  • We regularly hear from both customers and researchers that Bugcrowd feels like a family, and we strive to maintain that internally as well.
  • Our team consists of a broad range of people: musicians, adventure sports junkies, nature lovers, parents, cereal enthusiasts, night owls, cyclists, artists—you get the point.

At Bugcrowd, we are solving security threats and vulnerabilities that are relevant to everyone, therefore we believe solving these problems takes all kinds of backgrounds. We value the perspectives and experiences people from underrepresented backgrounds bring.

Disclaimer

This position has access to highly confidential, sensitive information relating to the technologies of Bugcrowd. It is essential that the applicant possess the requisite integrity to maintain the information in the strictest confidence.

The company is authorized to obtain background checks for employment purposes under state and federal law. Background checks will be conducted for positions that involve access to confidential or proprietary information (including trade secrets).

Background checks may include Social Security verification, prior employment verification, personal and professional references, educational verification, and criminal history. Applicants with conviction histories will not be excluded from consideration to the extent required bylaw.

jobs.excerpt: Job Summary: The Technical Advisor II – Malaria provides senior-level technical guidance to the AFGHS–FHI 360 core team, country programs, and national partners across the full scope of malaria programming.
jobs.description:
Job Summary:


The Technical Advisor II – Malaria provides senior-level technical guidance to the AFGHS–FHI 360 core team, country programs, and national partners across the full scope of malaria programming. The role provides technical leadership from project start-up and workplan development through implementation, ensuring technical quality across existing projects and new buy-ins. Reporting to the Senior Technical Advisor, Malaria, the Advisor provides technical support to country teams, ensures budgetary and regulatory compliance, and supporting the team in the country to engage donors and stakeholders on malaria-related matters. The Advisor supports country teams to implement evidence-based interventions at health facility and community levels, in alignment with national policies, covering malaria supply chain management, diagnosis, treatment, surveillance, and quality of care. This includes supporting countries in modernizing commodity planning and gap analysis tools to reflect MOU guidelines, new malaria commodities, Global Fund GC8 data, and available supply chain information. The Advisor provides oversight to an assigned portfolio, sets strategic priorities to guide resource investments in malaria and related technical areas, establishes and monitors best practices, and leads business development efforts. The role is accountable for contributing to the development and implementation of technical, strategic, and operational plans, goals, and policies to advance malaria programming.


Key Responsibilities

As part of the Technical Advisor II – Malaria's broader support to the malaria portfolio, the Advisor works with country teams to support the Ministries of Health, national malaria control/elimination programs (NMCPs/NMEPs), laboratories, and research partners to translate supply chain, clinical, prevention, and surveillance evidence into improved policies and services, particularly for underserved populations. Specific functions include:

1. Malaria Commodities, Supply Chain Coordination, and risk analysis:

  • Lead development of supply plans, including dashboards, risk summaries, and visual products that highlight current and projected stockouts, procurement delays, funding gaps, overstock, and expiry risks for internal and donor reporting.
  • Data Analysis & Risk Monitoring including collecting, validating, analyzing, and synthesizing forecasting, inventory, procurement, shipment, and consumption data; develop and maintain methodologies to track stock-out/overstock risks, expiries, pipeline gaps, and funding shortfalls; and monitor supply chain performance indicators to enable proactive mitigation.
  • Cross-Country Coordination: Produce country-level and cross-country commodity availability analyses and collaborate with technical, program, and country teams to ensure data consistency and timely reporting.

2. Malaria Case Management

  • Provide technical leadership for malaria case management strategies, guidelines, training, and implementation at health facility and community levels.
  • Advise national programs on accurate diagnosis and appropriate management of uncomplicated and severe malaria, malaria in pregnancy, and malaria in vulnerable populations.
  • Support evidence-informed introduction and monitoring of multiple first-line therapies (MFT), where appropriate, to help preserve antimalarial efficacy and manage resistance risks.

3. Malaria Prevention

  • Advise on ITN product selection, campaign and routine distribution strategies, coverage and use, and durability and bioefficacy monitoring, in collaboration with supply chain teams.
  • Support residual efficacy assessments, including cone bioassays, and timely corrective or mop-up actions where performance falls below agreed standards.
  • Lead technical support for context-appropriate introduction, implementation, evaluation, and potential scale-up of spatial emanators and other promising vector control tools.
  • Assess scientific evidence, PMI guidance, national regulatory requirements, product safety, acceptability, cost, and operational feasibility before recommending deployment.
  • Develop implementation protocols, monitoring indicators, learning agendas, and practical guidance with national programs, product developers, and research partners.

4. Country Technical Assistance and Quality Improvement

  • Provide remote and in-country support to country teams; review workplans, technical approaches, curricula, budgets, and monitoring plans.
  • Assess clinical and operational performance through field visits, supportive supervision, and mentorship; work with national partners to implement corrective actions.
  • Strengthen adherence to malaria diagnosis and treatment standards through clinical audits, job aids, quality indicators, and continuous quality improvement.
  • Facilitate cross-country learning and adaptation of effective practices.

5. Community Case Management and Integrated Service Delivery

  • Strengthen iCCM and referral pathways for malaria and common childhood illnesses, with emphasis on remote, mobile, displaced, and underserved populations.
  • Build community health worker capacity in fever assessment, authorized diagnostic testing, appropriate treatment, danger-sign recognition, pre-referral care, and referral follow-up.
  • Improve linkages between communities and facilities for supervision, reporting, commodities, and continuity of care; coordinate with maternal, newborn, child health, and nutrition teams.

6. Malaria Surveillance, Data Use, and Performance Monitoring

  • Work with surveillance, monitoring and evaluation, and health information teams to improve completeness, quality, interpretation, and use of case management data.
  • Support DHIS2 and other national reporting systems, dashboards, performance reviews, and routine use of diagnostic, treatment, referral, and outcome indicators.
  • Use epidemiological and program data to inform risk stratification, subnational tailoring, resource prioritization, and corrective actions.
  • Contribute to technical reports, evaluations, policy briefs, and learning products.

7. Partnerships, Innovation, and Program Development

  • Represent FHI 360, as requested, in malaria case management, surveillance, diagnostics, and therapeutic efficacy technical forums.
  • Build collaboration with Ministries of Health, NMCPs/NMEPs, WHO, donors, academic institutions, laboratories, and implementing partners.
  • Provide technical input to proposals, country strategies, new program designs, and operational research opportunities.
  • Assess emerging diagnostics, medicines, digital tools, and delivery approaches for safe, effective, and context-appropriate adoption; identify opportunities for integration with primary health care and global health security.

8. Technical and Professional Competencies

  • Sound knowledge of PMI malaria guidance, malaria supply chain system, prevention and case management, and iCCM.
  • Strong analytical, technical writing, facilitation, and presentation skills; ability to communicate scientific findings to policymakers and implementers.
  • Demonstrated ability to support multidisciplinary teams, manage competing priorities, build partnerships, and work effectively across diverse country contexts.
  • Commitment to scientific integrity, national ownership, safeguarding, and sustainable capacity strengthening.

Desired Professional Profile

  • The ideal candidate combines rigorous clinical and public health expertise with practical malaria program implementation experience, works effectively with senior government counterparts and frontline teams, and can translate emerging evidence into feasible improvements in service quality and treatment outcomes.

Required Qualifications

Education

  • Minimum master's degree in public health, infectious diseases, epidemiology, clinical medicine, or a closely related discipline. Clinical degree preferred.
  • Additional training in malaria surveillance, malaria in pregnancy, malaria vaccines, supply chain, or vector control is desirable; project management certification is an advantage.
  • Project Management (PM) Certification preferred.

Professional Experience

  • At least 12 years of progressively responsible experience providing technical leadership in malaria.
  • Demonstrated experience advising Ministries of Health and national malaria programs and developing case management policies, clinical guidelines, training materials, or quality improvement approaches.
  • Strong experience in malaria prevention, diagnosis and treatment, including facility- and community-based services, with experience integrating malaria services into maternal, newborn, and child health platforms.
  • Ability to analyze surveillance and program data and translate evidence into practical recommendations for policy and implementation.
  • Professional fluency in written and spoken English is required.
  • Proficiency in additional languages such as French an advantage.
  • Experience with major international donor-funded malaria programs and regional or multicountry technical assistance is an advantage.

Typical Physical Demands:

  • Typical office environment.
  • Ability to spend long hours looking at a computer screen and doing repetitive work on a keyboard.
  • Ability to sit and stand for extended periods of time. Ability to lift/move up to 5 lbs.

Technology to be Used:

  • Laptop, Microsoft applications (i.e., Office 365, SharePoint, Skype/Zoom/Teams), cell phone/mobile technology, and standard office equipment.

Travel:

  • 10 – 25% periodic international travel to malaria-endemic countries is required for technical assistance, program reviews, supervision, research collaboration, and partner engagement; frequency will depend on program needs.
